blocks.x: Quantum & Advanced Compute applied to Semiconductors & Hardware. This page sets out the operating context, the delivery pattern we run, the services and platforms involved, and the outcomes we commit to.

Hardware companies run the longest R&D loops under the sharpest IP threats: design simulation, fab yield (their own or partners'), supply-chain visibility and product security. Compute acceleration and governed data are the compounding assets.

At Technology & SaaS level this capability reads as: crypto-agility design for products holding customer secrets (enterprise PQC demands answered). The sub-industry page narrows it to the unit's workflows, regimes and KPIs.

Programs run on a fixed rhythm so progress is visible from week one. Weeks 1–2 lock the baseline: the current metric is measured with your team and signed before build starts. Weeks 3–8 deliver the pilot on bounded scope — one decision path, one workflow, one plant or one portfolio — with a control owner named on your side. Weeks 9–12 industrialize what worked: runbooks, monitoring, enablement and a measured delta against the signed baseline. Anything that misses its gate is stopped or redirected with a documented decision, not quietly extended.
